newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere to cancel shares worth $170 mln.
newsitem.headline: Solidere to cancel shares worth $170 mln.

text.p: Lebanon's biggest company Solidere said it plans to cancel shares worth about $170 million at an extraordinary shareholders' meeting due on Tuesday but likely to be postponed.
A simultaneous ordinary shareholders' meeting will be asked to approve a 25 cents dividend for 1996 -- 25 percent up on the 1995 dividend.
Company officials said the meetings were unlikely to get a quorum on Tuesday. A 66 percent quorum is needed for the extraordinary meeting and 50 percent for the ordinary meeting.
They will probably take place at the end of June and the dividend will be distributed in mid-July, the officials said.
Solidere executive David Mulville told Reuters that investors welcomed the plan to cancel shares.

Solidere's capital currently totals $1.17 billion A shares -- for distribution to property owners in the Beirut city centre that Solidere is redeveloping in exchange for their rights -- and $650 million B shares issued in a January 1994 flotation.
The shares to be cancelled are treasury stock A shares held by the company because they were not taken up by some property owners who preferred to redevelop their property rather than take shares.
The owners' decisions reduced Solidere's assets, leading to the board's decision to carry out a matching reduction of capital.

Mulville said the company believed this could help to improve investor perceptions of Solidere, whose share price on the Beirut Stock Exchange has been negatively affected by an excess supply of A shares and is currently languishing at low levels.

"The shares sitting on the balance sheet don't have an impact on the price (of Solidere shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange) but there is a perception that they could be reoffered in future," Mulville said.

"Therefore we want to make it clear now that we are reducing capital and it's better to cancel them now. By doing that we are increasing the proportion of representation of existing shareholders," he said.
"The move we are taking has been extremely well received, especially by international investors," he added.
Mulville said the lengthy process of distributing the A shares to the former owners was now nearing its end after after nearly three years.
"We are about 85 percent through the distribution process. Just under $1 billion worth of A shares have been issued out of $1.17 billion," he said.

"We have passed the peak. Volumes are now considerably less than last year. It's going to take some time to complete but it's less and less each day and the impact will be negligible in a few months," Mulville added.
